style.vernacular: Hill-slung capital at about 1,240 m in the Mdzimba Mountains: a compact town centre of 2-6 storey face-brick and cream-painted blocks around the Swazi Plaza pedestrian core, suburban bungalows and walled houses with red or green corrugated-iron and tile roofs on the slopes, granite outcrops showing through eucalyptus and jacaranda, and traditional grass-thatched beehive huts surviving in royal and cultural settings.
style.ornament: Swazi beehive-hut thatch forms and Emahlanga-style woven grass patterns used on craft and tourist buildings; national colours (blue, yellow, crimson) and the Sibebe-style granite boulder motif on municipal and royal-linked architecture; plain face-brick banding and shop-front awnings downtown.
